chunks: And in the narration of Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, peace be upon him:

Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام held the owner of the animal liable for what it trampled with its front legs and what it struck with its hind legs. So there is no liability upon him unless a person strikes it.

key_terms.صَاحِبَ الدَّابَّةِ: the owner or keeper of the animal
key_terms.نَفَحَتْ بِرِجْلَيْهَا: what it struck or kicked with its hind legs
key_terms.وَطِئَتْ بِيَدَيْهَا: what it trampled with its front legs

ai.seo_question: When is the owner of an animal liable for injuries caused by it in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about liability for harm caused by an animal. It states that the owner is held liable for damage caused by the animal’s trampling or kicking, except in a case where another person provokes the animal by striking it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5353 - In the narration of Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as):

"Indeed, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) held the owner of the animal liable for what it trampled with its front legs and what it struck with its hind legs. However, there is no liability upon him unless a person strikes the animal."
